at hoste.explanation: "At hoste" means "to cough". To say you have been coughing for a while: "Jeg har hostet i tre dage" (I have been coughing for three days).

at hugge.explanation: "At hugge" means "to chop". To say you chop firewood: "Han hugger brænde" (He chops firewood). To cut with a knife, use "at skære" (to cut): "Jeg skærer brødet" (I cut the bread).

at hulke.explanation: "At hulke" means "to sob". To say someone sobs hard: "Han hulkede i flere minutter" (He sobbed for several minutes). For ordinary crying, use "at græde" (to cry): "Barnet græder" (The child is crying).

at huske.explanation: "At huske" means "to remember". To remind someone to do something: "Husk at ringe" (Remember to call). To keep a fact in mind, use "at huske på" (to keep in mind): "Husk på, at det er farligt" (Keep in mind that it is dangerous).

at huske på.explanation: "At huske på" means "to keep in mind". To tell someone to bear a fact in mind: "Husk på, at det er farligt" (Keep in mind that it is dangerous). To say you remember a name, leave out "på" (on) and use "at huske" (to remember): "Jeg husker hans navn" (I remember his name).

at hvile.explanation: "At hvile" means "to rest", as in taking a break. To say you rest yourself for a moment, add "sig" (yourself): "Jeg hviler mig lidt" (I am resting a bit).

at hvile sig.explanation: "At hvile sig" means "to rest". It is "at hvile" (to rest) with "sig" (yourself). To say you relax, use "at slappe af" (to relax): "Jeg slapper af i sofaen" (I relax on the sofa).

at hviske.explanation: "At hviske" means "to whisper". To say who you whisper to, use "til" (to): "Hun hvisker til sin søster" (She whispers to her sister).

at hygge sig.explanation: "At hygge sig" means "to have a cozy / nice time". To wish someone that, say: "Hyg dig!" (Have a nice time!) To say who you had it with, use "med" (with): "Jeg hyggede mig med mine venner" (I had a nice time with my friends).

at hylde.explanation: "At hylde" means "to celebrate / honor". To say people honor a person: "De hylder vinderen" (They honor the winner). For a birthday or a holiday, use "at fejre" (to celebrate): "Vi fejrer min fødselsdag" (We celebrate my birthday).

at hyle.explanation: "At hyle" means "to howl". To say the wind howls: "Vinden hyler om huset" (The wind howls around the house).

at hyre.explanation: "At hyre" means "to hire". To say you rent something, use "at leje" (to rent): "Vi lejer en bil" (We rent a car).

at håbe.explanation: "At håbe" means "to hope". To name what you hope for, add "på" (on) before it: "håbe på en gave" (hope for a gift). To say you hope so, say: "Det håber jeg" (I hope so).

at håndtere.explanation: "At håndtere" means "to handle". It is built from "hånd" (hand). To say someone deals with complaints: "Hun håndterer klagerne" (She handles the complaints).

at hælde.explanation: "At hælde" means "to pour / lean". To say you pour a drink: "Jeg hælder mælk i glasset" (I pour milk into the glass). To say something slopes: "Taget hælder" (The roof slopes).

at hænge.explanation: "At hænge" means "to hang". To say you spend time with friends, use "hænge ud" (hang out): "Vi hænger ud efter skole" (We hang out after school).

at hænge op.explanation: "At hænge op" means "to hang up". When something is hung up, "op" (up) comes after it: "Han hænger jakken op" (He hangs the jacket up). To end a phone call, use "at lægge på" (to hang up): "Hun lagde på" (She hung up).

at hænge sammen.explanation: "At hænge sammen" means "to make sense / be connected". To say things are linked: "Alt hænger sammen" (Everything is connected). To say a story does not add up: "Historien hænger ikke sammen" (The story does not make sense).

at hævde.explanation: "At hævde" means "to claim". To report what someone says is true: "Han hævder, at han var hjemme" (He claims that he was at home). To report plainly what someone said, use "at sige" (to say): "Han siger, at han var hjemme" (He says that he was at home).

at hævde sig.explanation: "At hævde sig" means "to assert oneself". It is "at hævde" (to claim) with "sig" (oneself). Without "sig", it means "to claim": "Han hævder, at han er uskyldig" (He claims he is innocent).

at hæve.explanation: "At hæve" means "to raise / withdraw (money)". To say you raise a price: "hæve prisen" (raise the price). To say you raise your voice: "Hun hævede stemmen" (She raised her voice).

at hæve penge.explanation: "At hæve penge" means "to withdraw money". To say you put money in, use "at sætte penge ind" (to deposit money): "Jeg sætter 500 kroner ind" (I deposit 500 kroner).

at hævne.explanation: "At hævne" means "to avenge". It is related to the noun "hævn" (revenge). To say you take revenge yourself, use "at hævne sig" (to take revenge): "Hun hævner sig på ham" (She takes revenge on him).

at høre.explanation: "At høre" means "to hear". To say you have heard news: "Jeg har hørt, at han flytter" (I have heard that he is moving). To listen on purpose, use "at lytte" (to listen): "Jeg lytter til musik" (I listen to music).

at høre efter.explanation: "At høre efter" means "to listen". To tell children to pay attention: "Hør efter!" (Listen!) To say you hear a sound, use "at høre" (to hear): "Jeg hører en lyd" (I hear a sound).
